output.name: Morath
output.myth: Every house on the Spindle has a smoke-hole, and every smoke-hole has a rule. The smoke goes up straight from the hearth, the way a good line goes up from a reel, and climbs past the gulls. Then it stops, at a height no one has reached, like washing that forgot to dry. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, saw it the first time and said nothing. Kavet, the drop spindle, turns just north-west of it, still drawing her thread thin. Hirun, the gull who flew the string, sees it from the south-west and says it is only waiting. Aun, who cut the string, looked up and asked what was waiting there. The old women say it is waiting for someone to come home. Aun flew a sealskin kite up to find out. The smoke did not move for him, and he did not come down the same. Ketsa, the grey nanny at the edge, would not come in past the door-stones either. So when you light the fire at dusk, bank it low and keep the pot on. Mend your nets while it burns.
output.finding: From Ketsa, the grey nanny at the edge of the Spindle, look about one hand-span (18°) west and you will find Morath, the smoke that stops.
